messages:
mina: Heads-up — nightly eval (nightly-2028-07-05-03) shows a big regression for fa->zh when inputs contain mixed Persian + Chinese snippets. BLEU down ~9.2, chrF down ~0.18. Looks specific to the int4 quant profile we rolled Friday. :thinking_face:

sam: can you paste a minimal reproducer?

mina: sure — here's one of the failing cases from the prompt set:

```
input: "امروز به بازار رفتم و دیدم 小卖部 هنوز باز است."
expected_zh: "今天我去了市场，看到小卖部还开着。"
model_out (int4-profile): "今天我去了市场，而 小 卖 部 已 经 关闭。"
```

li: ugh. the model is flipping the Chinese fragment semantics and even spacing the Chinese chars oddly. looks like tokenization/byte-fallthrough for mixed-script sequence. :eyes:

arash: which model + quant combo? dedicated or hosted?

mina: model: rwd-7b-v2, serving variant: rwd-7b-v2-int4-lowmem (rolled 2028-07-02). On Dedicated pool eu-west-1.

eval-bot: nightly-2028-07-05-03 report attached — overall summary: fa->zh BLEU delta -9.2, en->zh -0.4, fa->en -0.3. Problem concentrated on mixed-script prompt subset (n=342).

li: i ran the tokenizer on the input — here's the tokenization dump (spaced for readability):

```
TOKENIZER (rwd-7b-v2-tokenizer):
["▁امروز", "▁به", "▁بازار", "▁رفتم", "▁و", "▁دیدم", "▁", "小", "卖", "部", "▁还", "▁开", "▁是", "."]
```

li: note the lone empty token ("▁") between Persian and Chinese — that separator is collapsing into a token that the runtime treats as ASCII whitespace and then quant execution path seems to mis-handle KV cache boundaries, producing dropped context for the Chinese span.

sam: could also be a kernel selection bug in the int4 path that triggers on non-Latin codepoints next to CJK. we saw similar heuristics for attention packing before but not this bad.

arash: assign bisect. mina, can you run eval-bisect pointing at the last known-good (rwd-7b-v2-int8-std) and the new int4 build? run with --subset mixed-script and --trace-tokens.

mina: starting now. command: `./tools/eval-bisect --id nightly-2028-07-05-03 --left rwd-7b-v2-int8-std --right rwd-7b-v2-int4-lowmem --subset mixed-script --trace-tokens --out /tmp/bisect-186240`

eval-bot: bisect job queued (job-49821). ETA ~12m.

li: quick patch idea: force tokenizer to emit explicit U+200E/200F directional markers around RTL/LTR boundary during preprocessing and see if symptom disappears. that would be cheap to try as a mitigation in the serving stack.

sam: I'd prefer to bisect first to prove root cause is quant kernel not tokenizer. If bisect points to int4 runtime, then try kernel workaround or fallback to int8 for mixed-script requests.

arash: good plan. mina please also capture a trace from runtime with KV cache offsets and token ids (use --dump-kv). we need to check whether cache indexing is off by one at script boundary.

mina: will do. I'll post bisect results + dump once job finishes. tagging @platform-oncall in case we need a hotfix to dedicated pool config. :bell:

sam: thanks — if this reproduces on a handful of examples, we should add a dedicated mixed-script regression test to nightly evals and gate int4 rollout.

li: noted. I'll draft the test and add to nightly prompt set (mixed-script-multilang-001).

mina: bisect finished: flag points to rwd-7b-v2-int4-lowmem build hash f3a7c9. Left (int8) ok, right (int4) fails on 98% of subset. Token traces show token id sequence mismatch at boundary in the runtime decode step. posting artifacts: /artifacts/bisect/job-49821/*.log

arash: confirm kernel-level regression. escalate to infra-ml for kernel selection rollback on int4 path. I'll open an infra issue and link artifacts.

sam: for immediate mitigation, please add a routing rule to map requests matching regex with mixed Persian/CJK to int8 pool for 24h. quick and safe.

mina: done — rule applied for eu-west-1 dedicated pool. monitoring now. :white_check_mark:

li: thanks everyone. once infra rolls back, we should run a controlled re-quant with extra tests for mixed-script edge cases. I'll own the coverage + prompt additions.

mina: closing thread for now — will post follow-ups when infra responds. :wave:
